title: Codefall test run
description: One run of one target: what was run, at which revision, what drove it, and what each criterion did. Written to .codefall/tests/<timestamp>-<run-key>.json beside the Markdown report of the same run. A suite or spec run fills `runner`; an agentic run fills `driver` and `variants`.

kind.description: case is one test case; suites is every declared suite; suite is one named suite; changed is the subset the changed files reach; epic is every case an epic's children name plus the changed subset, on the epic's branch.

key.description: The suffix of the filename stem, slugged: checkout-place-order, suites, suites-changed, or the suite's own name.

id.description: The case id — its path minus the extension, relative to test-cases/. Present for a case run.

ref.description: What the user typed, before resolution.

modality.description: The case's modality, or `suite` when the target is not a case. The PASS/FAIL/ERROR/PARTIAL vocabulary belongs to `agentic` alone.

commands.description: The commands that ran, as written.

commandSource.description: Where the commands came from: the verb's CUSTOMIZE.md, the project's AGENTS.md verification section, inference from the repository, or the Runners section of the testing root's AGENTS.md.

filter.description: For a changed-files run, the filter the changed paths mapped onto, or the reason the runner could not filter and the full suite ran.

epic.description: The epic bead whose work this run tested, when the target was an epic. The newest record carrying an epic is that delivery's last test run.

revision.description: HEAD of the checkout the run ran in.

branch.description: The branch checked out for the run, when it was not the default branch.

dirty.description: True when the working tree carried changes.

driver.description: The driver an agentic run used, as this session knows it.

tool.description: The tool that drove the run.

proof.description: The live call that proved it, and what came back.

runner.description: A suite or spec run's own result, in the runner's own vocabulary.

name.description: playwright, go-test, or whatever the project declared.

failures.description: Each failing test by name, with the runner's own message.

output.description: Path under the testing root's .artifacts/ where the full output landed. Never the output itself.

variants.description: One entry per variant run. An agentic run fills every field; a spec run of a multi-variant case may carry verdicts alone.

verdict.description: The agentic vocabulary. A spec run reports through `runner` instead.

citation.description: The criterion's source as the case file states it: SPEC-003-REQ-01-AC-01, or derived from SPEC-003-REQ-01.

evidence.description: What was observed, in one line, quoting what was on screen where that is the evidence.

attempts.description: Per-step attempt counts, recorded even when the step eventually succeeded.

sideEffects.description: Everything the run created against real services, recorded the moment it existed.

disposition.description: left means it still exists and the report says what remains to be done about it.

anomalies.description: The anomaly sweep: user-visible wrongness no criterion asked about. Never folded into the verdict.

triage.description: What each finding was classified as. The working notes stay git-ignored; the classification is part of the run's record.

subject.description: The criterion or anomaly this classifies, as the report names it.

class.description: Real bug, wrong expectation, flake, or agent variance.

priority.description: The Beads priority the finding carries and the bead filed for it takes: a real bug that fails a criterion P1, a wrong expectation P2, agent variance or an anomaly P3, a flake P4. P0 is set by a person, never by the verb.

occurrences.description: For variance, how often it has been seen across runs: "2 of 6 runs".

issue.description: The tracker issue it was filed on or commented on, when the user asked for one.

bead.description: The child of the epic filed beside the issue, when the run's target was an epic's work and the user asked for one.

notes.description: What the run could not do and why: a refused modality, a driver that did not prove, a suite the runner could not filter.
